name: White Celery Sauce
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: teacupful of broth in which the fowl is boiled
ingredients.originalText: 1 teacupful of broth in which the fowl is boiled

ingredients.name: Heaping tablespoonful flour, and same of butter
ingredients.originalText: Heaping tablespoonful flour, and same of butter

instructions.text: Boil the celery tender in salted water; drain, and cut into bits half an inch long.
Thicken the gravy from the fowl—a teacupful—with the flour; add the butter, salt, and nutmeg, then the milk.
Stir and beat until it is smooth; put in the celery; heat almost to boiling, stirring all the while; serve in a tureen, or, if you prefer, pour it over the boiled meat or fowls.

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Boil the celery tender in salted water; drain, and cut into bits half an inch long.
2. Thicken the gravy from the fowl—a teacupful—with the flour; add the butter, salt, and nutmeg, then the milk.
3. Stir and beat until it is smooth; put in the celery; heat almost to boiling, stirring all the while; serve in a tureen, or, if you prefer, pour it over the boiled meat or fowls.
